Traditional Lebkuchen

Served at: First Sunday of Advent

Makes about 4 dozen (48) cookiesPrep 30 min (plus 8-24 hours chilling)Cook 12-15 min per batch

Lebkuchen are classic German gingerbread-like cookies, deeply rooted in centuries of tradition. Their warm, spiced aroma and rich flavor make them an essential part of the Advent season, often enjoyed on the First Sunday of Advent as families begin their preparations for Christmas. These tender, chewy cookies are a delightful way to mark the start of the festive period.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup (57 g) unsalted butter
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2 1/2 cups (300 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) baking soda
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) ground cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) ground cloves
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) ground allspice
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon (1.25 ml) ground cardamom
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) finely chopped candied orange peel
  • 1/4 cup (35 g) finely chopped candied lemon peel
  • 1 cup (100 g) finely ground almonds or hazelnuts
  • For the Glaze:
  • 1 1/2 cups (180 g) powdered sugar
  • 3-4 tablespoons (45-60 ml) fresh lemon juice or water

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, combine the honey, brown sugar, and butter. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the butter is melted and the sugar is dissolved. Do not boil. Remove from heat and let cool to lukewarm.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until light and frothy. Gradually whisk in the cooled honey mixture.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, allspice, ginger, and cardamom.
  4. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Stir in the chopped candied orange peel, candied lemon peel, and ground almonds or hazelnuts.
  5. The dough will be very soft. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the dough to firm up.
  6. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough to about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thickness. Use a round or rectangular cookie cutter (about 2-3 inches / 5-7.5 cm) to cut out shapes. Reroll scraps as needed.
  8. Place the cut-out cookies about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart on the prepared baking sheets.
  9. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the cookies are set. They will be soft when hot but will firm up as they cool.
  10. While the cookies are baking or cooling, prepare the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice (or water) until smooth. Adjust the liquid to achieve a pourable but not too thin consistency.
  11. Once the cookies are slightly cooled, spread a thin layer of glaze over each Lebkuchen. Let the glaze set completely before storing.

Tips

  • For a richer spice flavor, prepare your own Lebkuchen spice mix by grinding whole spices just before use.
  • Lebkuchen improve with age; store them in an airtight container at room temperature for several days to allow the flavors to deepen and the cookies to soften.
  • You can decorate the glazed cookies with blanched almonds or candied fruit before the glaze sets for an extra festive touch.
